claim: Mirador del Fitu sits at 597 m on the AS-260 between Arriondas and Colunga, ~11 km from each, with a 360º panorama spanning the Sueve, Ponga, Picos de Europa and the Cantabrian coast; the concrete watchtower was inaugurated in 1927.
quote: The viewpoint stands at 597 meters in the Sierra del Sueve, offering a spectacular 360º vision... Take the AS-260 road connecting Arriondas and Colunga. The viewpoint is equidistant from both towns at approximately 11 kilometers away.

claim: Fitu has a small car park at the mirador and a larger gravel overflow lot ~100 m further up near telecom antennas; access is free, 24/7, but the road can close in snow/ice.
quote: There's a small car park right at the mirador and a second, larger gravel parking area 100 meters further up (next to some telecom antennas).

claim: The PR-AS 71 from Fitu to Pico Pienzu summit is 11.73 km out-and-back, ~700 m of elevation gain (577 m to 1,145 m), classified Dura (hard), 3-5 hours, passing the Majada de Bustacu shieling; vultures, choughs, Asturcón horses and fallow deer are commonly seen.
quote: It is common to see vultures, choughs, Asturcón horses and fallow deer, the faunistic symbol of the Sierra del Sueve.

claim: The Sierra del Sueve is the last refuge of the Asturcón, an ancient muscular pony about four feet tall that the Romans used in mine work; its dark herds roam the high pastures freely.
quote: the asturcón, one of the world's oldest horses, a muscular and agile animal just four feet high, whose dark wild herds blend into a dark green landscape.

claim: Plan Lagos 2026 closes the CO-4 to private cars 24 h/day on Easter (28-31 Mar), most of Apr (1-12, 18-19, 25-30), May weekends + 1 May, daily 1 Jun-18 Oct (with exceptions), 24-25 + 31 Oct, 1-2 Nov, and 1-8 Dec; access then is by €9 round-trip shuttle from P1 Cangas bus station / P2 El Bosque / P3 Muñigu / P4 Repelao / P5 El Peregrino, parking €2.
quote: During the regulated period, the access road to the Lakes will remain closed to traffic from 00:00 to 24:00.

claim: The Plan Lagos shuttle buses do not stop at Mirador de la Reina; on regulated days you reach it only by taxi (which will halt on request, ~€10/adult round trip) or by bike — outside regulated periods or before the 8:30 am cutoff, drive up the CO-4 and park in the dedicated lot at the mirador.
quote: Unfortunately, the buses do not stop at the Mirador on their way to the Lakes.

claim: Mirador de la Reina sits at 910 m altitude roughly 8 km up the CO-4 from the Basilica of Covadonga, giving a wide circular panorama over the northern Picos de Europa, the Güeña valley meadows and, on clear days, the Bay of Biscay.
quote: Mirador de la Reina... 910 metros de altitud... amplio panorama circular de los Picos de Europa y vistas... Onís, Cangas de Onís y Covadonga.

claim: The Pico Pienzu summit (1,159 m, highest in the Sueve) returns coast-to-mountain views from the Picos to the Bay of Biscay with Gijón, Ribadesella, Colunga and Villaviciosa visible below; the trail starts directly at Fitu's car park.
quote: Picu Pienzu standing as the highest peak in the Sierra del Sueve at 1,159 meters... panoramic vistas range from the Picos de Europa mountains to the Bay of Biscay

claim: The CO-4 climb up to Mirador de la Reina includes sustained 12-14% grades, with the steepest precipice-edged stretch continuing beyond the mirador toward the Lakes — relevant for nervous drivers and cyclists.
quote: At the Mirador de la Reina there are slopes of 13% and 14%
